correctness.rationale: Every nonzero rank-one R on A=k[t]/(t^n) factors as R(a)=φ(a)u, u≠0. Substitution into weight-zero Rota–Baxter equation forces u²∈ku and φ∘μ_u scalar multiple φ; nilpotence in the local algebra excludes nonzero scalar eigenvalues and scalar-unit image, yielding u²=0 and φ(uA)=0. For ν(u)=r this is equivalent to r≥ceil(n/2) and φ killing (t^r). Hence the reduced rank≤1 locus is the union of rank-one determinantal cones X_r⊂Hom(A/(t^r),(t^r)), each geometrically irreducible of dimension n-1, with Segre projectivizations. For r<s, intersections have Hom(A/(t^r),(t^s)) rank≤1, dimension n-1-(s-r), making all X_r proper irreducible components. Distinct valuation strata have q^(n-r-1)(q^r-1) maps, so nonzero count is floor(n/2) q^(n-1) - (q^floor(n/2)-1)/(q-1). Independent exhaustive F2 multiplication and basis-pair Rota–Baxter checks for n=2,3,4 yielded 1,3,13 maps and agreement with formula; the rank-one algebraic proof covers all fields and all n≥4.

originality.rationale: Farooq 2026 arXiv:2605.15670 addresses DIFFERENT square-zero radical truncation K[x_1,..,x_m]/m² over characteristic zero, not univariate k[t]/t^n with n>=4 or finite fields. Guo-Rosenkranz-Zheng 2014 classify order two/three semigroup algebras and polynomial k[x] monomial/injective operators, not these rank-one reduced moduli. The standard Segre determinantal geometry is not novel by itself; claim is the exact Rota–Baxter cutout, its irreducible components and intersections, and its all-q census. Published Resultary exterior algebra over F2 is another nonisomorphic four-dimensional algebra.
residual_risks: A general rank-one RB criterion in an older local-algebra paper might make the geometry a corollary without explicit enumeration.
All-field proof concerns the REDUCED locus; unreduced Rota–Baxter scheme could have embedded or nilpotent structure not classified.
